---
title: NVIDIA NIM Embeddings
guide-section: Building a Store
bread-crumbs: false
---

`EmbeddingNVIDIA` uses [NVIDIA NIM](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia) embedding models. You can use NVIDIA's hosted API or run a NIM container on your own GPUs. With a self-hosted container, documents and queries are sent to your own server for embedding.

## Installation

`EmbeddingNVIDIA` uses the `openai` client library included with raghilda, so no additional packages are needed.

To use NVIDIA's hosted API, create an account at [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia), generate an API key, and set it in the environment:

```bash
export NVIDIA_API_KEY="nvapi-..."
```

The provider reads `NVIDIA_API_KEY` automatically. You can also pass `api_key=` directly. The key is not saved with the store, so set the environment variable when reconnecting.

## Basic usage

Create a provider with the model you want to use. These examples use [`nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b`](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b):

::: {#0f0ec18a .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingNVIDIA

provider = EmbeddingNVIDIA(model="nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b")
```
:::


Pass it to a store with the `embed=` argument:

::: {#ce42bd58 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingNVIDIA

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="my_store.db",
    embed=EmbeddingNVIDIA(model="nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b"),
)
```
:::


`DuckDBStore.create()` sends a short string to the embedding API to determine the number of values in each embedding.

## Choosing a model

See [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com/search?q=embed) for available models. raghilda currently defaults to `nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-1b-v2`, whose [hosted endpoint has been deprecated](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-1b-v2). Set `model=` explicitly when using NVIDIA's hosted API, as in the examples above.

Check the model's page for its embedding dimensions and input length limit. You can also check the number of dimensions by embedding a short string:

::: {#f864b976 .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
provider = EmbeddingNVIDIA(model="nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b")
print(len(provider.embed(["test"])[0]))
```
:::


::: {.callout-note}
Use the same model for documents and queries so their embeddings can be compared. To change models, create a new store and ingest the documents again.
:::

## Query and document embeddings

NVIDIA's embedding API uses an input type to distinguish search queries from documents. raghilda maps `EmbedInputType.QUERY` to `"query"` and `EmbedInputType.DOCUMENT` to `"passage"`. The store sets the input type automatically: chunks added with `upsert()` or `ingest()` use the document type, and text passed to `retrieve()` uses the query type.

When calling the provider directly, use `input_type=` to specify the type of text:

::: {#b38e4233 .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingNVIDIA, EmbedInputType

provider = EmbeddingNVIDIA(model="nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b")

doc_embeddings = provider.embed(
    ["HNSW is a graph-based approximate nearest-neighbor index."],
    input_type=EmbedInputType.DOCUMENT,
)

query_embedding = provider.embed(
    ["How do vector indexes work?"],
    input_type=EmbedInputType.QUERY,
)
```
:::


When `input_type` is left out, the provider assumes `EmbedInputType.DOCUMENT`.

## Self-hosted NIM containers

NVIDIA publishes Docker images that serve NIM models on your own hardware. Once a container is running, point the provider at it with `base_url=`:

::: {#75ad22bf .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingNVIDIA

provider = EmbeddingNVIDIA(
    model="nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-1b-v2",
    base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1",
)
```
:::


Set `model` to the model served by the container. The client library requires an API key value even if your server does not require authentication. In that case, set `NVIDIA_API_KEY` to a placeholder:

```bash
export NVIDIA_API_KEY="not-used"
```

Set this environment variable when reconnecting as well. The store saves `base_url`, so it will keep sending requests to your container.

See [NVIDIA's NIM documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/) for instructions on pulling and running the containers.

## Handling long inputs

NVIDIA's API rejects inputs that exceed the model's length limit by default (`truncate="NONE"`). To remove tokens from the end of an input until it fits, set `truncate="END"`:

::: {#3a0a53ef .cell execution_count=6}
``` {.python .cell-code}
provider = EmbeddingNVIDIA(model="nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b", truncate="END")
```
:::


Text removed by truncation is not included in the embedding. You can also use smaller chunks to keep inputs within the model's limit; see [Chunking](chunking.qmd).

## Batching and rate limits

`EmbeddingNVIDIA` sends texts in batches of 20 by default. Use `batch_size=` to change how many texts are sent in each request.

If the API returns a rate-limit error (HTTP 429), the provider retries with increasing delays. If the retries fail, it raises the error.

## Reconnecting to a store

When you connect to an existing store, raghilda restores the provider's model, `base_url`, batch size, and truncation setting:

::: {#cb744866 .cell execution_count=7}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore

store = DuckDBStore.connect("my_store.db")
```
:::


Set `NVIDIA_API_KEY` before reconnecting; the API key is not saved.

## Parameters

The constructor defaults are listed below. For NVIDIA's hosted API, set `NVIDIA_API_KEY` and choose an available model with `model=`.

| Parameter    | Default                                 | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`      | `"nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-1b-v2"`   | NVIDIA embedding model name                                                                     |
| `base_url`   | `"https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1"` | API endpoint. Change this for a self-hosted NIM container                                       |
| `api_key`    | `None`                                  | API key. Falls back to the `NVIDIA_API_KEY` environment variable                                |
| `batch_size` | `20`                                    | Texts per API call                                                                              |
| `truncate`   | `"NONE"`                                | How to handle inputs that exceed the model's limit: `"NONE"` raises an error, `"END"` truncates |

For API details, see the [`EmbeddingNVIDIA` reference page](/reference/embedding.EmbeddingNVIDIA.qmd).

## Complete example

This example builds a store from two web pages, then searches it. Replace the example URLs with pages you want to search:

::: {#d2eeaa8b .cell execution_count=8}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingNVIDIA
from raghilda.read import read_as_markdown
from raghilda.chunker import MarkdownChunker

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="docs.db",
    embed=EmbeddingNVIDIA(model="nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b", truncate="END"),
    name="docs",
    title="My Documentation",
    overwrite=True,
)

chunker = MarkdownChunker()
for url in ["https://example.com/doc1", "https://example.com/doc2"]:
    store.upsert(chunker.chunk(read_as_markdown(url)))

store.build_index()

chunks = store.retrieve("How do I configure authentication?", top_k=5)
for chunk in chunks:
    print(chunk.text[:200])
```
:::


To use a self-hosted container, set the provider's `base_url=` and `model=` to match the server, as shown [above](#self-hosted-nim-containers).

## Using NVIDIA with ChromaDB

When you pass `EmbeddingNVIDIA` to `ChromaDBStore`, raghilda adapts it to ChromaDB's embedding interface. Queries and documents use their respective input types, and the provider is restored when you reconnect from Python. ChromaDB clients in other languages cannot use this Python embedding function. See [ChromaDB Embedding Functions](chromadb-embedding-functions.qmd) for details.
